summary: Note placement is one search now — settle each note, sweep until a pass moves nothing — where it used to be an exhaustive 8^n grid below two notes and a single settling pass above. A full check of all eleven diagrams does 91 fewer layout candidates for one more browser start, and no diagram's placement changed.
why: The grid's justification no longer reproduced, and two notes had become the dearest count a diagram could have — dearer than three or four. Sweeping reaches the grid's answer on all 42 two-note diagrams measured, at 22 candidates against 64, and gives three- and four-note diagrams the better search too.
